titleEn: The Song of the Cid — The Cid's second claim: the three thousand marks (tirada 137, lines 3199–3249)
part: Tirada 137 (third part) · The Cid's second claim: the three thousand marks (lines 3199–3249)

sentences.i: Then my Çid the Campeador rose: “Thanks be to the Creator, and to you, my lord king! I am satisfied now as to my swords, Colada and Tizón.
sentences.n: Tirada 137, continued (assonance ó: Campeador, señor, Tizón, Carrión …) — the Çid's second demand: the wealth he gave the Infantes with his daughters; the Infantes are hard put to pay (Pidal: Segunda demanda del Cid. El ajuar de sus hijas. Los infantes hallan dificultad para el pago (the last word damaged on the scan, read pago) — 'Second demand of the Cid. His daughters' trousseau. The Infantes find it hard to pay'). Pidal's rubric calls the money el ajuar, the trousseau (the bride's parents' gift, axuvar in the poem); the poem itself says only averes, 'goods, wealth' (v. 3206), and it is not the arras, the husband's settlement. Pidal begins v. 3199 with a paragraph indent: the swords have been handed over (end of the last part), and the Çid rises again. Luego, 'then, next'. se levantó, 'rose' (levantarse). Grado al Criador, 'thanks to the Creator' (grado, 'gratitude', as at v. 3035). rey señor, 'lord king', the title and the address side by side. ya pagado so de mis espadas, 'now I am satisfied as to my swords': pagado, 'paid, content' (pagar, 'to satisfy'); so = soy, 'I am'. de Colada e de Tizón, the two swords the Infantes have just given back.

sentences.i: I have another grievance against the Infantes of Carrión: when they took my two daughters away from Valencia, I gave them three thousand marks in gold and silver;
sentences.n: Otra rencura he de, 'I have another grievance against' (rencura, 'grievance, complaint'; he, 'I have'; de of the party complained of). ifantes de Carrión, without the article, as usual. quando sacaron de Valençia, 'when they took out of Valencia' — the journey that ended in the oak-wood of Corpes. mis fijas amas a dos, 'my daughters, both of them' (amas = ambas; fijas, f- for h-). tres mill marcos, 'three thousand marks' (the mark a weight of silver or gold; mill = mil). les dio, 'I gave them': Pidal's note to v. 3204: 'dio, "di yo"' — 'dio, "I gave"': Pidal's 'di yo' makes dio first person, 'I gave' (perhaps di with yo run on), not 'he gave'; Pidal prints it without an accent.

sentences.t:
yo faziendo esto ellos acabaron lo so;
denme mi[o]s averes quando mios yernos non son.”
sentences.l:
I doing this they carried-out the their-own;
let-them-give-me my goods since my sons-in-law not they-are.”
sentences.i: while I was doing this, they were carrying out their own design. Let them give me back my wealth, since they are my sons-in-law no longer.”
sentences.n: yo faziendo esto, 'I doing this', an absolute gerund: 'while I was doing this' (faziendo, f- for h-). ellos acabaron lo so: Pidal's note to v. 3205: 'acabaron, "llevaron a cabo, hicieron"' — 'acabaron, "carried out, did"'. lo so, 'what was theirs, their own (business)': the neuter lo with the possessive so; what they carried out is left unsaid — their plan against the daughters ('design' in the English is our reading). denme = den + me, 'let them give me' (present subjunctive of dar). mi[o]s averes, 'my goods, my wealth', the o of the first mios Pidal's restoration (averes, aver as a noun, 'possessions'; here the money). quando, 'since' (causal, as often). mios yernos non son, 'they are not my sons-in-law': the outrage at Corpes has broken the marriages.

sentences.t:
Aquí veriedes quexarse ifantes de Carrión!
Dize el co[m]de don Remond: “dezid de ssí o de no.”
sentences.l:
Here you-would-have-seen complain-themselves infantes of Carrión!
Says the count don Remond: “say of yes or of no.”
sentences.i: Here you would have seen the Infantes of Carrión protest! Count Remond says: “Answer yes or no.”
sentences.n: Pidal begins v. 3207 with a paragraph indent. Aquí, 'here, at this point'. veriedes, 'you would have seen' (conditional of veer), the minstrel turning to his listeners. quexarse, 'complain, protest' (quexar, x = [ʃ]). co[m]de don Remond, 'Count Remond' (house), the m Pidal's restoration; he is one of the two judges named at v. 3135. dezid de ssí o de no, 'say yes or no' (dezid = decid; de ssí o de no, 'of yes or of no'; the ss of ssí a spelling of the join after de).

sentences.t:
Essora responden ifantes de Carrión:
“Por essol diemos sus espadas al Çid Campeador,
que al no nos demandasse, que aquí fincó la boz.”
sentences.l:
Then answer infantes of Carrión:
“For that-to-him we-gave his swords to-the Çid Campeador,
that other-thing not of-us he-should-demand, that here ended the claim.”
sentences.i: Then the Infantes of Carrión answer: “We gave the Çid Campeador back his swords for this very reason, that he should claim nothing else from us: here his claim came to an end.”
sentences.n: Essora, 'then'. Por essol = por esso + le, 'for that … to him', the le cut to l and glued on; the Çid is then named again (al Çid Campeador). diemos = dimos, 'we gave'. sus espadas, 'his swords', Colada and Tizón. que al no nos demandasse, 'that he should demand nothing else of us' (al, 'other thing'; demandasse, imperfect subjunctive). que aquí fincó la boz, 'that here the claim ended' (house: finca la boz 'the claim ends'). Pidal's note to v. 3211: 'fincó la boz, como en 3167. Los infantes alegan que el Cid debió hacer su demanda de una vez, en un solo acto. La práctica formalista exigía que el demandante expusiese consecutiva e inmediatamente todos los puntos de la demanda, so pena de perder su derecho. Por eso es necesario que los alcaldes o jueces y el rey mismo autoricen esta segunda parte de la demanda civil del Cid, en los v. 3212-14, y que el Cid se ponga otra vez de pie y repita la demanda (3215) que antes se juzgó inútil' — 'fincó la boz, as at 3167. The Infantes plead that the Cid ought to have made his demand all at once, in a single act. Formalist practice required the plaintiff to set out all the points of his demand one after another and at once, on pain of losing his right. That is why the judges and the king himself must authorize this second part of the Cid's civil demand, in vv. 3212–14, and why the Cid stands up again and repeats the demand (3215) that had before been judged void.'

sentences.t:
Allí les respondió el comde do Remond:
“Si ploguiere al rey, assí dezimos nos:
a lo que demanda el Çid quel recudades vos.”
sentences.l:
There to-them answered the count do Remond:
“If it-should-please the king, thus say we:
to that-which demands the Çid that-to-him you-answer you.”
sentences.i: Then Count Remond answered them: “If it please the king, this is our ruling: you must answer him on what the Çid demands.”
sentences.n: Line 3211b is printed wholly in Pidal's italic: a whole line he restores. It is unnumbered in his edition, and the letter b is ours, not his (as with 3179b); he gives no footnote for it. Allí, 'there, thereupon'. el comde do Remond, 'Count Remond' (house): do for don, as printed (as at v. 3036); comde is so spelt here, co[m]de at v. 3208, conde at v. 3237. Si ploguiere al rey, 'if it should please the king' (ploguiere, future subjunctive of plazer). assí dezimos nos, 'thus we say' — the judges give their ruling (nos, 'we', the judges). a lo que demanda el Çid, 'to what the Çid demands'. quel = que + le, 'that … him'. recudades, 'you answer', present subjunctive of recudir: Pidal's note to v. 3213: 'recudadas, "respondáis", "deis satisfacción"' — '"that you answer", "that you give satisfaction"' (his headword is printed recudadas, a slip for the recudades of the text). vos, 'you', the Infantes, repeated at the line's end. So the second demand is allowed, as Pidal's note to v. 3211 says it must be.

sentences.t: Dixo el buen rey: “assí lo otorgo yo.”
sentences.l: Said the good king: “thus it I-grant I.”
sentences.i: The good king said: “I grant it so.”
sentences.n: otorgo, 'I grant, consent' (otorgar); yo, 'I', stressed at the line's end. The king confirms the judges' ruling, the authorization Pidal's note to v. 3211 speaks of.

sentences.i: The Çid Campeador rose to his feet: “This wealth I gave you — will you give it back to me, or give an account of it?”
sentences.n: Levantós = levantó + se, 'he rose', the se cut to s and glued on. en pie, 'to his feet'. Pidal's note to v. 3215: 'El Cid se dirige ahora directamente a los infantes y no a los alcaldes, como antes. Esta alternativa, según observa Hinojosa, representa una transición entre el procedimiento germánico primitivo, en que el juicio era una lucha entre las partes, a la cual asistían los jueces casi como meros espectadores, y el posterior, en que la intervención de los jueces era más eficaz' — 'The Cid now turns directly to the Infantes, and not to the judges as before. This alternation, as Hinojosa observes, marks a transition between the primitive Germanic procedure, in which the trial was a struggle between the parties at which the judges were present almost as mere spectators, and the later one, in which the judges took a more effective part.' Destos averes que vos di yo, 'of these goods that I gave you', the topic set first; the line is short, as printed. si me los dades: Pidal's note to v. 3216b: 'Sobre la conjunción si, véase 1922' — 'On the conjunction si, see 1922'; and there: 'La conjunción si encabeza una interrogación directa (como si fuese indirecta: dime si es pagado), 3216' — 'The conjunction si heads a direct question (as if it were an indirect one: tell me whether he is satisfied), 3216.' So si here is not 'if' but asks: 'will you give them to me?' (dades, present; 'if' kept in the literal line). o dedes dello razón, 'or give an account of it' (dedes, present subjunctive of dar; dello = de ello; razón, 'account, reckoning', our rendering of dar razón). The number 3216b is Pidal's own.

sentences.t:
Essora salien aparte ifantes de Carrión:
non acuerdan en conssejo, ca los averes grandes son:
espesos los han ifantes de Carrión.
sentences.l:
Then were-going-out apart infantes of Carrión:
not they-agree in council, for the goods great are:
spent them they-have infantes of Carrión.
sentences.i: Then the Infantes of Carrión go aside: they cannot agree on what to do, for the sum is great, and they have spent it.
sentences.n: Pidal begins v. 3217 with a paragraph indent. salien = salían, 'were going out', an imperfect among presents (the poem's tense-mixing). aparte, 'aside, apart'. non acuerdan en conssejo: Pidal's note to v. 3218: '"no convienen en la solución, no hallan salida"' — '"they do not agree on the solution, they find no way out"' (conssejo, 'deliberation, counsel'). ca, 'for'. los averes grandes son, 'the goods are great'. espesos los han: Pidal's note to v. 3219: '"los han gastado"' — '"they have spent them"': espesos, past participle of espender, 'to spend' (cf. espendiésteslo, v. 3238), agreeing with los (the averes). ifantes de Carrión closes both v. 3217 and v. 3219.

sentences.t:
Tornan con el conssejo e fablavan a sso sabor:
“Mucho nos afinca el que Valençia gañó.
quando de nuestros averes, assíl prende sabor;
pagar le hemos de heredades en tierras de Carrión.”
sentences.l:
They-return with the counsel and they-spoke at their pleasure:
“Much us presses he who Valençia won.
since of our goods, so-him takes desire;
pay him we-shall of estates in lands of Carrión.”
sentences.i: They come back with their counsel and speak as they please: “He who won Valencia presses us hard, since he has such a craving for our wealth; we will pay him in landed estates in the country of Carrión.”
sentences.n: Tornan … e fablavan, 'they return … and spoke', present and imperfect side by side. con el conssejo, 'with their counsel', what they had settled among themselves. a sso sabor, 'at their pleasure, as they liked' (sso = so, 'their'). Mucho nos afinca, 'he presses us hard' (afincar, 'to press, urge'; fincar, 'to plant firm'). el que Valençia gañó, 'he who won Valencia' (gañó = ganó): the Çid not named — perhaps scornfully, our reading. Pidal prints a full stop after gañó inside the speech, kept as printed; the sense runs on. quando de nuestros averes, assíl prende sabor: Pidal's note to v. 3222: '"cuando así le domina el deseo de nuestras riquezas"' — '"since the desire for our riches so masters him"'. assíl = assí + le, the le cut to l and glued on; prende sabor, 'takes relish, conceives a desire' (prender, 'to take'). pagar le hemos = le pagaremos, 'we will pay him', the split future with the pronoun between the infinitive and the ending (hemos). de heredades, 'with estates' (heredad, 'inherited landed property'). en tierras de Carrión, 'in the lands of Carrión' — far from Toledo, and not money.

sentences.i: When the Infantes had owned the debt, the judges said: “If that should please the Çid, we do not forbid it; but by our judgement this is what we order: that you pay it back here, within the court.”
sentences.n: alcaldes, 'judges'. quando manfestados son: Pidal's note to v. 3224: '"cuando hubieron confesado", esto es, "cuando reconocieron su deuda"' — '"when they had confessed", that is, "when they acknowledged their debt"': manfestados = manifestados, 'declared, confessed'; the subject is the Infantes, and the participle with son has the active sense 'they have confessed'. esso, 'that', the payment in lands. non gelo vedamos nos, 'we do not forbid it him' (gelo = ge + lo, ge the old form of le before lo; vedar, 'to forbid'). mas en nuestro juvizio, 'but in our judgement': Pidal's note to v. 3226: 'juvizio, "juicio", como en 3239, 3259' — 'juvizio, "judgement", as at 3239, 3259' (his italic z looks like an s in this type). assí lo mandamos nos, 'thus we order it'. que aquí lo enterguedes, 'that you pay it back here' (enterguedes = entreguéis, the r moved): Pidal's note to v. 3227: '"que le reintegren o le paguen aquí"' — '"that they reimburse him or pay him here"' (his gloss in the third person, the verse in the second). dentro en la cort, 'within the court': in the court, then and there — set against the lands of Carrión offered just before (our reading of the point).

sentences.t:
A estas palabras fabló rey don Alfons:
“Nos bien la sabemos aquesta razón,
que derecho demanda el Çid Campeador.
sentences.l:
At these words spoke king don Alfons:
“We well it know this matter,
that right demands the Çid Campeador.
sentences.i: At these words King Alfonso spoke: “We know this matter well: the Çid Campeador's demand is just.
sentences.n: Pidal begins v. 3228 with a paragraph indent. rey don Alfons, 'King Alfonso' (Alfons, the short form, as throughout). Nos, 'we', the king speaking of himself (or of himself and the court). la sabemos aquesta razón, 'we know it, this matter': the object said twice, la … aquesta razón (aquesta = esta; razón, 'matter'). que derecho demanda, 'that he demands what is right' (derecho, 'right, justice'), set first.

sentences.t:
Destos tres mil marcos los dozientos tengo yo;
entramos me los dieron ifantes de Carrión.
sentences.l:
Of-these three thousand marks the two-hundred hold I;
both to-me them gave infantes of Carrión.
sentences.i: Of these three thousand marks, two hundred are in my hands: the Infantes of Carrión, the two of them, gave them to me.
sentences.n: tres mil marcos: mil with one l here, mill at v. 3204, as printed. los dozientos, 'two hundred (of them)' (dozientos = doscientos). tengo yo, 'I hold'. entramos = entrambos, 'both'. Pidal's note to v. 3232: '"entrambos infantes me los dieron". Hinojosa opina que estos dozientos marcos son el regalo que el marido hacia, en señal de gratitud, al que le transmitía la potestad sobre la mujer, según el antiguo derecho germánico, en especial el de los Lombardos y Escandinavos. El rey habia casado a las hijas del Cid y ahora, disuelto el matrimonio, no quiere retener ese regalo. Los infantes pagan su deuda descontando los 200 marcos, v. 3246; pero luego el Cid perdona al rey la devolución y aun le añade más regalos de su parte, v. 3502' — '"both Infantes gave them to me". Hinojosa holds that these two hundred marks are the gift the husband made, in token of gratitude, to the one who handed over to him authority over the wife, under the old Germanic law, especially that of the Lombards and the Scandinavians. The king had married off the Cid's daughters, and now that the marriage is dissolved he does not wish to keep that gift. The Infantes pay their debt with the 200 marks counted off, v. 3246; but later the Cid excuses the king from returning them, and even adds more gifts of his own, v. 3502.'

sentences.i: I mean to give them back to them, since they are so ruined, so that they may pay my Çid, who was born in a good hour; since they have to pay, I do not want them.”
sentences.n: Tornárgelos quiero = quiero tornárgelos, 'I wish to give them back to them': not a split future but querer + infinitive, set in the same order (infinitive first), with the pronouns glued to the infinitive — ge (= le, 'to them', the Infantes) + los (the marks). ca, 'for, since'. t[a]n d[e]sfechos son, 'they are so ruined', the a and the e Pidal's restorations (desfechos = deshechos, f- for h-). enterguen a mio Çid: Pidal's note to v. 3234: '"paguen a mio Cid", como en 3227' — '"let them pay my Çid", as at 3227' (enterguen = entreguen, present subjunctive, the r moved). el que en buen ora naçió, 'he who was born in a good hour' (house). quando, 'since'. los an a pechar, 'they have to pay them' (aver a + infinitive, 'to have to'; an = han; pechar, 'to pay what is owed'). non gelos quiero yo, 'I do not want them (from them)': gelos = ge + los, the ge here the persons the marks would come from.

sentences.t:
Ferran[d] Go[n]çál[v]ez [odredes qué] fabló:
“averes monedados non tenemos nos.”
sentences.l:
Ferran[d] Go[n]çál[v]ez [you-will-hear what] spoke:
“goods coined not have we.”
sentences.i: Fernando González — you shall hear what he said: “Coined money we have none.”
sentences.n: Pidal begins v. 3236 with a paragraph indent. Ferran[d] Go[n]çál[v]ez, 'Fernando González' (house), the d, n and v Pidal's restorations; the manuscript form kept in the literal line. [odredes qué], 'you will hear what': the whole phrase Pidal's restoration, in his italic, with no footnote (odredes = oiréis, future of oír, the minstrel's aside). fabló, 'spoke' (f- for h-). The number 3236b is Pidal's own. averes monedados, 'coined wealth', that is, cash (monedado, 'coined, minted'). non tenemos nos, 'we do not have', nos stressed at the end.

sentences.t:
Luego respondió el conde don Remond:
“el oro e la plata espendiésteslo vos;
por juvizio lo damos antel rey don Alfons:
páguenle en apreçiadura e préndalo el Campeador.”
sentences.l:
At-once answered the count don Remond:
“the gold and the silver spent-it you;
by judgement it we-give before-the king don Alfons:
let-them-pay-him in valuation and let-take-it the Campeador.”
sentences.i: Count Remond answered at once: “The gold and the silver — you spent it; this is the judgement we give before King Alfonso: let them pay him in goods at a valuation, and let the Campeador take it so.”
sentences.n: Luego, 'at once'. el conde don Remond, 'Count Remond' (house), conde so spelt here. el oro e la plata espendiésteslo vos, 'the gold and the silver, you spent it': espendiésteslo = espendiestes + lo (espender = expender, 'to spend'; -estes, the old ending of the 2nd plural preterite, = gastasteis); lo, neuter, gathers the gold and the silver; vos, 'you', stressed at the end. por juvizio lo damos, 'we give it as judgement' (juvizio, 'judgement', Pidal's note to v. 3226). antel = ante + el, 'before the'. páguenle = paguen + le, 'let them pay him': the count turns from speaking to the Infantes to ruling about them. en apreçiadura: Pidal's note to v. 3240: 'apreçiadura, "especie (opuesto a dinero), cosas equivalentes a una cantidad de moneda"; abajo se expresa que las apreciaduras en que pagan los infantes son caballos, armas y vestidos' — 'apreçiadura, "kind (as against money), things equivalent to a sum of coin"; below we are told that the apreciaduras in which the Infantes pay are horses, arms and clothes' (the second apreciaduras printed without the cedilla). préndalo, 'let him take it' (prender).

sentences.t: Ya vieron que es a fer ifantes de Carrión.
sentences.l: Now they-saw that it-is to do infantes of Carrión.
sentences.i: The Infantes of Carrión saw now that it had to be done.
sentences.n: Pidal begins v. 3241 with a paragraph indent. Ya vieron, 'now they saw'. es a fer, 'it is to be done' (ser a + infinitive; fer = hacer, the short infinitive). Pidal's note to v. 3241: '"Ya vieron que hay que hacerlo", esto es, que no hay más remedio que pagar' — '"Now they saw that it has to be done", that is, that there is nothing for it but to pay.'

sentences.t:
Veriedes aduzir tanto cavallo corredor,
tanta gruessa mula, tanto palafré de sazón,
tanta buena espada con toda guarnizón;
recibiólo mio Çid commo apreçiaron en la cort.
sentences.l:
You-would-have-seen bring so-many horse swift,
so-many stout mule, so-many palfrey of season,
so-many good sword with all fitting;
received-it my Çid as they-valued in the court.
sentences.i: You would have seen them bring in so many swift horses, so many sturdy mules, so many palfreys in prime condition, so many good swords with all their fittings; my Çid took it all at the value set on it in the court.
sentences.n: Veriedes, 'you would have seen', the minstrel's aside again. aduzir, 'bring, lead in' (= aducir). tanto/tanta with a singular noun, 'so many a': tanto cavallo corredor, 'so many a swift horse'; tanta gruessa mula, 'so many a stout mule'. palafré, 'palfrey', the riding horse for the road, not the warhorse; de sazón, 'in prime condition', probably. guarnizón, 'fittings, mounting' (= guarnición), the sword's mounting. recibiólo, 'he received it' (lo, neuter, all of it), printed without the cedilla, and commo, as printed. apreçiaron, 'they valued, appraised' (apreçiar; the subject unnamed: whoever priced the goods in the court). These are the apreciaduras of Pidal's note to v. 3240: horses, arms and clothes.

sentences.t:
Sobre los dozientos marcos que tenia el rey Alfons
pagaron los ifantes al que en buen ora nació;
sentences.l:
Over the two-hundred marks that held the king Alfons
paid the infantes to-him who in good hour was-born;
sentences.i: Over and above the two hundred marks that King Alfonso held, the Infantes paid him who was born in a good hour;
sentences.n: Sobre, 'over and above, besides': the two hundred marks the king held (v. 3231) count towards the three thousand, and the Infantes pay the rest — Pidal's note to v. 3232: 'Los infantes pagan su deuda descontando los 200 marcos, v. 3246' — 'the Infantes pay their debt with the 200 marks counted off'. tenia, 'held', without an accent, as printed; no punctuation after Alfons, as printed. al que en buen ora nació, 'him who was born in a good hour' (house); nació without the cedilla here, against naçió at v. 3234, as printed.

sentences.t: enpréstanles de lo ageno, que non les cumple lo s[o].
sentences.l: they-lend-them of the others'-property, for not to-them suffices the their-own.
sentences.i: they borrow from others, for their own wealth does not suffice.
sentences.n: enpréstanles = enpréstan + les, 'they lend them', the subject unnamed — 'people lend to them', that is, they borrow (our reading of the impersonal plural). de lo ageno, 'of what is another's' (ageno = ajeno; lo, the neuter article). que, 'for'. non les cumple, 'does not suffice them' (cumplir, 'to be enough'). lo s[o], 'their own' (lo so, as at v. 3205), the o Pidal's restoration, in his italic; the s is roman.

sentences.t: Mal escapan jogados, sabed, desta razón.
sentences.l: Badly they-escape made-game-of, know-ye, from-this matter.
sentences.i: They come out of this affair badly, made fools of — be sure of it.
sentences.n: Mal escapan, 'they come off badly'. jogados, participle of jogar (= jugar, 'to play'): 'played with, made sport of, mocked' is our reading; Pidal gives no note on the page, and the sense is uncertain — it might rather be 'played out, worsted', as a loser in a game. sabed, 'know ye', the minstrel to his listeners. desta = de esta. razón, 'affair, matter'. The part and tirada 137 end here. Tirada 138 begins at v. 3250 with a new assonance (á), and the Çid, his civil demand ended, goes on to the challenge (Pidal's rubric to 138: Acabada su demanda civil, el Cid propone el reto — 'His civil demand ended, the Cid proposes the challenge').
